messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT: METRICS_SCRAPE_503 spike fired for service=eu-scrape-proxy (3 targets failing) — autopage to eng-sre. PD incident: https://pd.example.com/inc/INC12345

jessica: acked — I'm taking this. Seeing a bunch of 503s + nginx rate-limit warnings in scrape-proxy logs.

oncall-sre: copying. can you paste the log lines? also checking pod CPU.

jessica: logs show repeated limit_req hits, e.g.:
```
2026/03/15 14:23:12 [warn] 12345#0: *6789 limiting requests, client: 10.0.12.34, server: exporter-frontend, request: "GET /metrics HTTP/1.1", host: "exporter", ref: "-"
2026/03/15 14:23:13 [error] 12345#0: *6791 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.0.12.34, server: exporter-frontend, request: "GET /metrics HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.2.3.4:9100/metrics", host: "exporter"
```

ryan: adding context: we rolled a small change to exporter-frontend ~2h ago that bumped prometheus scrape concurrency. possible surge.

jessica: confirmed kubectl top shows scrape-proxy pods at ~95% CPU and high RPS. log-ingest queue for eu region shows backlog +420k events.

jessica: mitigation step 1: temporarily scale scrape-proxy to 4 replicas to absorb burst. running: `kubectl scale deployment/scrape-proxy -n infra --replicas=4`

oncall-sre: executed by me, pods are spinning up (scrape-proxy-3/4 ready). tailing logs now.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: page auto-escalated to leo (team lead) due to 5m without full mitigation.

leo: joining. is this customer visible? severity?

jessica: partial customer impact: dashboards for EU tenants are delayed or missing panels (timing out scrapes). CS notified one enterprise customer. maria-support, can you confirm customer outreach?

maria-support: confirmed — opened a ticket INC-9876 and sent an initial notification to the affected EU customers with status "investigating".

ryan: suggestion: add a short-term rate-limited scrape cache in front of exporter-frontend (nginx/varnish) to smooth spikes, and revert the concurrency change if scaling doesn't hold. also consider bumping nginx limit_req burst temporarily.

jessica: trying bump to limit_req burst=200 for now. applying via k8s configmap patch. snippet: 
```yaml
data:
  nginx.conf: |
    limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=one:10m rate=50r/s;
    server {
      location /metrics {
        limit_req zone=one burst=200 nodelay;
      }
    }
```

oncall-sre: applied configmap and rolled scrape-proxy one pod at a time. new logs showing much fewer limit_req warnings. 503 rate down from 60/s to ~2/s.

jessica: monitoring Prometheus: scrape_failures{region="eu"} dropping. log-ingest queue length decreased ~70% in last 7 minutes.

leo: good. mark incident as mitigated-ish but keep it open for RCA. we'll do a full postmortem — likely a combined regression + infra capacity mismatch.

jessica: I'll keep watch for 30m and then hand off to next oncall at 15:00 UTC. action items:
- revert exporter-frontend concurrency change if we see another spike
- implement short-term scrape caching/proxy in eu region
- add a prometheus alert for nginx rate_limit spikes (new rule)
- CS follow-up to affected customers with ETA

maria-support: customers have been notified; will provide updates after 30m if stable.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress. autoclose escalation suppressed for 30m.

jessica: tagging for RCA owners @ryan @leo. Filing an internal ticket with logs and timeline.

oncall-sre: handing off at 15:00 UTC to @ryan (next rotation). leaving monitoring runbook link: https://wiki.example.com/runbooks/scrape-proxy-backpressure

jessica: thanks all. will update PD and close page once we confirm stable for 30m.

leo: thanks — great triage. postmortem to include why nginx rate limits were low-priority on playbook and why deploy change lacked load-test run for scrapes.
